title: Collatz: sparse returns, identity atoms, and rigidity attempts
body:
## Current checkpoint

**Checkpoint 14 pursued four direct closing routes. It obtained no new universal closing estimate or Lean closing theorem.** The earlier positive sparse-return results remain in this PR. This continuation retains the exact arithmetic needed by a possible closing proof, a concrete obstruction to one attempted estimate, and the precise unsupported steps in the literature applications.

[Latest research packet](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/longshot/README.md) · [Source pins and review record](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/reports/2026-11-23-high-variance-attacks/README.md)

## Why this continuation

PR178 now has a stronger polynomial actual-window occupation bound. PR185 supplies same-source comparison uniform over all inverse horizons; PR175 and PR180 preserve the actual anchored stopping mass and full-denominator cycle arithmetic. I used those advances to test closing implications instead of pursuing another occupation-rate refinement. Exact input heads are recorded in the report.

## 1. Full-denominator identity atom

For D=2^A−3^p>0, let N_r(A,p) count binary words with ordered numerator C_w congruent to r modulo the whole D. On Z/DZ, let P0 and P1 be the permutation matrices of x↦x/2 and x↦(3x+1)/2. The exact unnormalized identity is

    [z^p] trace((P0+z P1)^A) = D N_0(A,p).

The strict bound < A D for A≥3 would exclude nontrivial positive cycles, because a primitive cycle supplies A distinct rotations. **That bound is not proved.** The trace identity keeps the distinguished zero residue and every prime power in D; it is an interface, not an exclusion theorem.

Uniform mixing is not a substitute: the fixed-weight law has too small a support at the relevant horizon. The inspected affine cutoff theorem has different parameter, independence and time hypotheses. Rotation balance also isolates zero and therefore supplies no bound on its mass.

[Exact argument, edge cases and attempted estimates](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/longshot/cycles/IDENTITY_ATOM_ATTEMPT.md)

## 2. A concrete failed monotonicity step

At (A,p)=(35,22), D=2,978,678,759 and r=2,209,100,811 is a unit modulo D. Two distinct coordinatewise comparable one-position lists have

    C_u = r+44D  = 133,270,966,207
    C_v = r+233D = 696,241,251,658.

Thus C_v−C_u=189D. Fibers need not be antichains, even at a unit residue. This refutes that proposed monotonicity step, not the stronger conjecture max_r N_r(A,p)<A.

Two complete fixed-weight enumerations tested 225,792,840 words at (32,20) and 1,476,337,800 at (35,22), with maximum fibers seven and nine and empty zero fibers. Four larger rational-denominator slices were also counted; they are not complete word laws. The exact scripts, raw outputs and coverage boundaries are retained. A separate small verifier independently recovers the complete nine-word displayed fiber from 86,283 candidate numerators.

[Recorded commands and scope](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/longshot/cycles/RUNS.md) · [Witnesses](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/longshot/cycles/maxfiber_35_22.json)

## 3. Direct escape and rigidity attempts

- [Adelic mixing and simultaneous approximation](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/longshot/ADELIC_MIXING_ATTEMPT.md): the unconditioned mixing theorem does not give the required conditional estimate at q_j mod 3^(j+r+1) with the matching real-height window. The natural real/binary/ternary Subspace product equals the original endpoint p exactly, with no negative-height saving; the growing center also changes the forms.
- [Canonical sibling mass](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/longshot/NONLOCAL_SIBLING_ATTEMPT.md): nonlocal routing and minimality did not yield OPEN-F/OPEN-S. The near-contact regeneration rederived during this pass was identified by independent review as a consequence of checkpoint 8 and is explicitly attributed as existing work.
- [Mahler rigidity](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/longshot/MAHLER_RIGIDITY_ATTEMPT.md): the exact Berg–Meinardus mixed equation generates an unbounded extraction hierarchy. No finite rank or pair of separate Mahler equations was proved, so the Adamczewski–Bell/Schäfke–Singer theorem cannot yet be applied. Pólya–Carlson does not eliminate the natural-boundary alternative.

## Standalone questions

- [Finite affine-word count](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/longshot/FINITE_AFFINE_WORD_QUESTION.txt): full definitions, the exact zero-fiber target, stronger all-residue option, and concrete failed shortcuts, without the application.
- [Mixed-decimation rigidity](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/longshot/MIXED_DECIMATION_QUESTION.txt): the exact 0/1 sequence relations and the missing finite Mahler equations, without assuming finite-state closure.

## Earlier positive checkpoint retained

[Checkpoint 13](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/fdcb137214f4be8ac30dbb025d6eeb6568e22e2a/research/lean-global-resolvent-20261121/overview/returns/README.md) proves an explicit actual finite core M_0(S,h)=6^h 2^[4S(4S+3h)] and an effective source-uniform O_S(N/log N) low-run occupation bound. Its separate Evertse argument proves that a nonexceptional sparse return within any fixed multiple of log n forces an input below n^eta, for every fixed 0<eta≤1 and sufficiently large n. Fourteen finite supporting Lean statements were audited there; the complete orbit arguments and literature inputs have written-proof scope. PR178's newer polynomial occupation rate is credited in checkpoint 14. Earlier checkpoints remain indexed by the research README.

## Verification and limits

- Independent agent review checked the trace normalization, genuine itinerary, primitive/trivial edge cases, and the contact-subtraction argument and attribution.
- The primary agent inspected the argument and enumeration sources, freshly recovered the nine-word witness fiber, checked all recorded integer ranges and slice bounds, and verified the source/text manifest.
- No new Lean declarations or axioms are added in checkpoint 14; its written and computational results are not labeled kernel proofs.
- Clean complete-checkout validation passed on both the local tested tree and the actual published commit, covering 587 tracked files. The five repository gate commands exited 0. This is integrity validation, not mathematical verification.
- Published commit: ff3e068fa44eb85bb918580b2e10e18c027a18e6. Tested and published tree: f9222ad73581a051d36b5a831478766b934b140f. The remote tree exactly matches the local tested tree.

Full Collatz remains open. The live arithmetic target is an exact zero-specific coefficient bound; the escape targets still require a pointwise estimate at the retained ordinary source or the unproved finite closure in the generating-function route.
